messages:
devon: incident-bot just paged us — Severity: S2. Inference-edge 5xx spike in eu-west-1 (metric: 5xx_rate x10 baseline). I'm primary until 08:00 UTC. Priya is secondary. I'm starting triage now; posting quick handoff + runbook links so folks can jump in. 

incident-bot: PAGE: [S2] inference-edge / eu-west-1 — 5xx spike. 1200 failures in last 5m. Pager: oncall@redwood. Logs: https://observability.redwood/alerts/2654321000 

devon: Quick checklist I'm following (in order):
1) Verify if it's a code/regression vs infra: check pod OOMs and recent deploys (Console -> Deploys).
2) If OOM / memory pressure, drain /restart offending pods and route traffic to fallback model.
3) If latency/backpressure, reduce batch_size and enable fallback model route.
4) Customer-impact triage (Carol) — list top clients and error rates.

Runbooks / links: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/inference-5xx-checklist 
Fallback routing runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-fallbacks 
KV-cache fallback: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-eviction
Metrics: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/inference-edge 
Logs (live tail): https://logs.redwood/query?alert=2654321000

devon: Quick remediate steps I'm about to run (will comment when done):
```bash
# 1) identify pods with OOM/killed restarts
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | egrep "OOM|CrashLoopBackOff"
# 2) evict problematic pod safely (let k8s spin up replacement)
kubectl -n inference drain pod/inference-edge-abc123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# 3) toggle fallback route (console CLI)
redwood-cli routes update inference-edge --fallback-model small-quantized-v1 --enable-fallback
```

priya: SG, I'm standing by. If you want me to swap into primary, ping me with `takeover` and I'll claim. I'll prep the pre-warm capacity for the fallback model and start warming 2 nodes (eu-west-1). Also I'll open a canary evaluation run for 50 rps to validate quality. :eyes:

alex: A few quick diagnostics to consider if drain doesn't help: check JVM native memory and GPU memory logs. If model server is OOMing due to KV cache, try forcing KV cache eviction: 
```bash
# instruct sidecar to drop KV cache (one-off)
kubectl exec -n inference deployment/inference-edge -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/kvcache/evict
```
Also look at recent commit hashes in the last deploy: console -> deploys -> inference-edge -> commits. If a deploy went out ~5-10m before page, roll back to prior revision as last resort.

mike: If traffic spike is the root cause, we can enable temporary rate-limiting and light-touch model downgrade: 
1) Flip route flag to route 20% traffic to small fallback: 
`redwood-cli traffic-split set --route inference-edge --split fallback=20`
2) Rapidly reduce default batch size via feature-flag: 
`redwood-cli feature-flag set --key inference.batch_size --value 4 --env eu-west-1`
I'll stand by to execute with you, Devon. Also I can bump auto-scale min replicas by +2 to absorb burst.

carol: Customer-impact note: top failing customers (by request count): acme-inc, beta-startup, gamma-LLM. I'm drafting a short internal status and will open SOC ticket for any enterprise customers affected. If you need me to notify account teams, say so. I'll also pull SLA hit metrics.

devon: Update - I performed pod drain on node inference-edge-04; new pod spun up but is still reporting 5xx for a subset of requests. I'm going to flip the fallback route to 20% and start KV cache eviction on the new pod. If that reduces 5xx we'll ramp.

devon: Executed commands:
```bash
# flipped fallback
redwood-cli routes update inference-edge --fallback-model small-quantized-v1 --enable-fallback && redwood-cli traffic-split set --route inference-edge --split fallback=20
# trigger KV eviction
kubectl exec -n inference deployment/inference-edge -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/kvcache/evict || true
```

alex: Nice, watch the error rate and p95 latency. If p95 is climbing >2s it's probably queuing. Consider pre-warming more fallback replicas. Also check worker queue length: https://observability.redwood/metrics/queue-length?env=eu-west-1

priya: Fallback is healthy at 20% so far, 5xxs dropped ~60% in last 2m. I'll continue warming and prepare to increase to 50% if we regress.

carol: Logged impacted customers and sent short note to account teams for acme-inc and beta-startup. No external status yet until we confirm stability.

devon: Plan for next 15m: monitor 5xx_rate and p95; if stable, gradually increase fallback to 50% and then rollback any problematic deploys if needed. If you have spare cycles please review the runbook pages above and post any additional quick remediation snippets here. :thumbsup:

mike: Can help with scaling; will stand by for an ops go.

incident-bot: RESOLVE: Alert 2654321000 — 5xx spike reduced below threshold. Duration: 18m. Summary: partial fallback + KV eviction reduced failure rate.

devon: Closing loop — marked resolved in console and updated the incident ticket. Will file a short post-incident note with root-cause guesses and follow-ups (deploy gating, better pre-warm heuristics). Thanks all.
